newsitem.title: ITALY: Shuttle train to cut France-Italy travel time.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle train to cut France-Italy travel time.

text.p: A new rail shuttle link that will cut the travelling time between the northern Italian city of Turin and Paris by 85 minutes was inaugurated on Friday.

The shuttle, which begins regular service on Sunday, is a joint operation between Italy's FS state railway, using its high-speed "Pendolino" rolling stock, and the high-speed TGV trains of France's SNCF state railway.

The service will reduce the journey time between Turin and Paris to five hours and 20 minutes and Turin to Lyon to three hours and 50 minutes. It will also cut one hour off the Milan-Paris journey, making it six hours and 40 minutes.

The inaugural shuttle left Turin's Porta Nuova station at 12:20 p.m. (1020 GMT) on Friday and was due to arrive in Lyon shortly after 4 p.m. (1400 GMT), after reaching speeds of up to 200 km per hour (125 mph) on some stretches.
The shuttle is part of a rail cooperation project aimed at managing the connections between France and Italy. The rolling stock will be owned by the respective national railway networks.
